queer_characters.name: Danielle
queer_characters.notes: Described explicitly as a 'directionless young bisexual Jewish woman' who has relationships with both a male sugar daddy and her ex-girlfriend Maya; framed as an authentic exploration of identity and self-worth, called one of the best bisexual films by a critic.

queer_characters.name: Maya
queer_characters.notes: Danielle's ex-girlfriend and a love interest she reconnects with; her prior relationship with Danielle is stated in the plot, but no specific label for Maya is given so the queer umbrella is used.

queer_creators.name: Emma Seligman
queer_creators.notes: Writer-director who drew on her own bisexuality when developing the character of Danielle, per the source text.

contributor_notes: Danielle's bisexuality is explicit in the source text and drawn from writer-director Emma Seligman's own experience (own-voices). Maya is confirmed as an ex-girlfriend but given no specific label, so tagged under the queer umbrella; a maintainer may refine. Content warnings noted in source (sexual content/nudity, sex work references, infidelity, anxiety-inducing tension) do not map cleanly to the available trigger_warnings enum, so that array is left empty. Ending described as hopeful/healthier path, hence happy-ending. Subtitle and audio language info not provided.
